title: Every planning change rescans the whole project's work items and edges to check for cycles, so its cost grows with closed history
outcome: Every planning change rescans the whole project's work items and edges to check for cycles, so its cost grows with closed history
acceptance: The cycle check after an ordinary prerequisite add, a decomposition, a supersession or an atomic plan reads a bounded quantity that does not grow with the project's completed, cancelled or superseded history, proven by a test that adds a large closed history to a project and asserts the check's row visits stay within the same bound as the same live graph without that history
Cycle detection still refuses every cycle it refuses today, covered by the existing acyclicity tests
